text:
alex: Heads-up — running long-context perf harness on Dedicated and Hosted. Dedicated instances show steady KV cache growth over ~1h runs, hosted plateaus. attaching short trace and jemalloc output :thinking_face:

alex: repro steps: use longchat benchmark (ctx=64k tokens), batching=auto, kernel=auto, kv_policy=adaptive. baseline on hosted vs dedicated vs onprem.

alex: snippet from jemalloc (Dedicated, after 45m):
```
arena_0: allocated: 12.3G, active: 10.8G, metadata: 120M
kv_slots: total_frames=1.2M, pinned=38k, free_frag=420M
page_faults: 342K
```

tasha: interesting. on Hosted we see less fragmentation? what are the NUMA settings and hugepage config on Dedicated nodes?

kevin: Dedicated is using 2-socket machines with default numactl (interleave disabled). Hugepages off by default. Onprem GPU boxes had 1-socket NVLink machines with 2MB hugepages enabled.

sana: also noticed VPC MTU on some dedicated clusters is 1500 vs 9000 on hosted. could that affect page alignment/copy patterns for our MMAP-backed KV store? :eyes:

jordan: MTU affecting MMAP alignment seems odd, but we do see more syscalls and smaller TCP segments which increases kernel scheduler jitter in our throughput traces. that can change batching behavior and make more frequent small writes to cache backing store.

alex: i captured a short perf script showing increased minor faults and write syscalls on Dedicated. truncated:
```
# Dedicated (45m)
minor_faults  count: 320k
write_calls    count: 78k
# Hosted (45m)
minor_faults  count: 80k
write_calls    count: 15k
```

tasha: wow, 4x minor faults. can someone rerun with `--kernel=avx512-optimized` pinned vs auto? maybe kernel selection is causing different memory access patterns (e.g., smaller working set per thread).

kevin: running that now on a dedicated staging pool (job 4729). infra-bot: please post the job link when ready.

infra-bot: job 4729 queued -> https://ci.internal/jobs/4729 :white_check_mark:

kevin: results (quick): avx512 kernel reduces minor faults by ~30% but KV growth still present. it slows growth slope, not eliminate.

sana: could be KV reuse heuristic timing-sensitive. if batching heuristics adapt slower under jitter, we may end up creating more KV frames and not reusing them promptly. check our "idle-sweep" window config (default 60s).

alex: i dug into logs — we see a bursty pattern where many short-lived contexts allocate new KV frames instead of appending to existing ones. timeline: 0-10m normal, 10-25m gradual increase, 25-40m step-up when a canary workload starts causing different token lengths.

jordan: hypothesis: Dedicated's NUMA placement + kernel selection -> higher syscalls -> batching heuristic decreases target batch size -> more frequent evict/reserve cycles -> fragmentation -> slower reuse and apparent leak.

tasha: action items: 1) run the same longchat with hugepages enabled on Dedicated, 2) run with numa interleave=all, 3) instrument KV allocator with epoch sampling to track per-tenant frame churn.

kevin: started runs: HP on, NUMA interleave on, and a control with forced batch_size=32. infra-bot will post links.

infra-bot: job 4735 (hugepages) started, job 4736 (numa-interleave) started, job 4737 (fixed-batch-32) started.

sana: if fixed batch eliminates growth then it's batching adaptation bug. if hugepages helps, fragmentation alignment is likely root cause. if numa helps, placement and mem-bind matters. all three could interact.

alex: also flagging customer-impact: one Dedicated tenant hit OOM earlier today in staging while hosted remained fine. going to pause deploys to that pool until we confirm. :lock:

jordan: can we add jemalloc decay tweaks as a temporary mitigation? decrease epoch to force faster free? small config change while we investigate.

tasha: agree. i'll ship a short-lived rollout with MALLOC_CONF="decay_time:10,metadata_thp:always" on the staging pool post-haste.

kevin: early results: hugepages run shows 60% drop in free_frag and KV slot compaction appears better. fixed-batch run eliminates growth entirely but increases p99 latency by ~8%. numa-interleave reduced growth by ~20%.

alex: great. summary: primary drivers seem to be alignment/fragmentation (hugepages helps) and batching adaptation (fixed batch stops growth at cost of latency). NUMA has secondary effect.

sana: next steps: 1) propose default: enable hugepages on Dedicated GPU pools and add an adaptive batching floor (min_batch=16) to avoid pathological small-batch churn. 2) instrument per-frame reuse counters and add alert if growth rate > X MB/min. 3) prep customer rollback playbook.

tasha: i'll draft the RFC for enabling hugepages + min_batch floor and include perf numbers. assigning to eng-runtime for review.

alex: thanks team. i'll file an incident ticket for the tenant OOM and link this thread. feel free to ping me for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
